claim.property: object-class predictability (4-class Seal/Tablet/Pottery/Other; secondary 2-class Seal-vs-Tablet) of the sign sequence, measured as per-object accuracy
claim.protocol: temporal held-out: model fitted ONLY on M77 (1977) corpus, scored on deduplicated post-1977 objects (CISI-numbered not-M77-attested + Dholavira + Lothal), seal-identity dedup, no held-out sequence/identity in training
claim.baselines: tuned per-class Kneser-Ney 3-gram (same M77 data) AND a SIGIL-style class-conditional position-unigram control (matched on unigram+length)
claim.test: paired bootstrap p<0.001 (10,000, seed 20261117) at pooled AND Mohenjo-daro AND Harappa separately (n>=20 each)
claim.label: structural finding (object-type predictability across the 1977 time split), never decipherment

verdict_per_comparator.claims: modal ending sign takes 28-45% of endings (in-sample, 1977-era corpus)
verdict_per_comparator.reason: a re-derivation of an in-sample ending-frequency statistic; not a held-out predictive property, not object-type, not a time split

verdict_per_comparator.claims: terminal-class joint ending share 50-75% (in-sample)
verdict_per_comparator.reason: in-sample terminal-class frequency; no held-out, no object-type, no baselines-vs-control test

verdict_per_comparator.claims: zero-violation terminal-zone (R1) compliance 65-82%, >=25pts above within-text shuffle (in-sample)
verdict_per_comparator.reason: in-sample compliance of a rule; the null is a within-text shuffle, not a held-out + KN + SIGIL-control design; property is rule-compliance, not object-type prediction

verdict_per_comparator.claims: pre-enumerated stroke taxonomy contains >=1 family (>=3 members, monotone freq, final-rate<5%) (in-sample)
verdict_per_comparator.reason: stroke-family existence in-sample; not a temporal held-out prediction

verdict_per_comparator.claims: double-terminal endings (distinct signs) 4-18% of eligible texts (in-sample)
verdict_per_comparator.reason: in-sample ending-pattern frequency; not object-type, not held-out

verdict_per_comparator.claims: [initial-class]->[high-freq strictly-medial] bigram in corpus top10 (in-sample)
verdict_per_comparator.reason: in-sample bigram ranking; the structure claim is a multi-position object-type likelihood, not a single bigram

verdict_per_comparator.claims: final-position entropy (Miller-Madow) lower than initial by >=0.3 bits (in-sample)
verdict_per_comparator.reason: in-sample positional-entropy gap (the published positional finding); the structure claim's property is object-type accuracy on held-out, and it is NOT the edge-entropy statistic that SIGIL shows is non-specific

verdict_per_comparator.claims: foreign texts: elevated mean per-text surprisal under a home model (in-sample + foreign sub-corpus)
verdict_per_comparator.reason: surprisal on foreign (non-home) texts; a different property (language-likelihood) and a different population (foreign vs post-1977 home material)

verdict_per_comparator.claims: emblem-animal vs terminal-distribution weighted JSD <0.10 bits (in-sample; the emblem is independent)
verdict_per_comparator.reason: an emblem/text INDEPENDENCE statement (JSD small); the structure claim is object-type predictability, an orthogonal property (and the field-symbol lens p2 is the emblem angle, judged negative)

verdict_per_comparator.claims: plain jar text-final >=60% / marked jar <=15% (in-sample, both transcriptions)
verdict_per_comparator.reason: in-sample jar-final rate; not object-type, not held-out

verdict_per_comparator.claims: count paradigm starts at three (values 3-8 : 1-2 >= 8:1) (in-sample)
verdict_per_comparator.reason: in-sample numeral-value distribution before the tree; not object-type prediction

verdict_per_comparator.claims: emblem independence: no sign-by-field-symbol pair survives BH-FDR 5% after dedup (in-sample, >=500 seals)
verdict_per_comparator.reason: the FALSIFIED emblem linkage (in-sample). The field-symbol lens (p2) is the closest relative and is judged NEGATIVE; the object-type claim does not involve the emblem at all

verdict_per_comparator.claims: seals and sealings do not co-locate (>=80% different site) (in-sample)
verdict_per_comparator.reason: a co-location rate; not object-type, not a time split

verdict_per_comparator.claims: >=20% of distinct seal texts have a one-substitution twin, differing before the ending (in-sample)
verdict_per_comparator.reason: in-sample twin rate (the ligature lens p3 is the closest relative, judged negative on the held-out); not object-type

verdict_per_comparator.claims: stability over time: jar-final and opener rates differ <=10pts between earliest/latest dated periods (in-sample, dated sub-corpora)
verdict_per_comparator.reason: the closest comparator — a TIME effect — but it measures in-sample rate STABILITY (a difference bound) across dated periods of the 1977-era corpus, not a predictive held-out accuracy beating two baselines. Different statistic (|rate_early - rate_late| <= bound) and different direction (we predict, they bound). NOT equivalent.

verdict_per_comparator.claims: blind validator for any proposed dictionary (any sign-to-sound key must beat scrambled + value-shuffled nulls)
verdict_per_comparator.reason: a DICTIONARY (sound-key) validator; the structure claim is explicitly NOT a decipherment/dictionary (object-type, not sign-to-sound)

verdict_per_comparator.claims: repetition avoidance, foreign person-sign openers, no home opener abroad, marker exclusivity, closed title slot, voucher values (all frozen for NEW data, in-sample-derived)
verdict_per_comparator.reason: frozen new-data predictions about specific sign/position properties (repetition, openers, co-occurrence); none is object-type prediction with a time split + dual baselines + site replication

verdict_per_comparator.claims: the 1977 concordance/tables: sign positions, frequency, site/object tabulation (in-sample, 1977)
verdict_per_comparator.reason: descriptive 1977-era tables; no predictive held-out model, no 2026 post-1977 test, no KN/SIGIL baselines

verdict_per_comparator.claims: structural statistics on the EBUDS subset (reciprocity, connectivity, beginner/ender asymmetry, non-randomness) (in-sample)
verdict_per_comparator.reason: in-sample corpus-level statistics (the kind SIGIL shows is non-specific); not a temporal predictive object-type property

verdict_per_comparator.claims: 179 MD unicorn seals: 98.3% uniqueness, edge-peaked positional entropy, stroke numerals 15.4% penultimate, digit-2 = 66.9% of numerals, 8 one-substitution pairs; 'registration codes / credit instruments'
verdict_per_comparator.reason: in-sample on a 179-seal CISI-vol-3 sub-corpus; the properties are uniqueness / edge-entropy / numeral-position (all in the non-specific class per 2608.02999) — none is a temporal M77->post-1977 predictive object-type accuracy beating a tuned KN + SIGIL control. The 'credit instrument' reading is an interpretation, not the predictive structural claim.

verdict_per_comparator.claims: the standard Indus statistics (uniqueness, directional asymmetry, positional/lexical/entropy/predictive/network measures) are reproduced by a non-linguistic generative emblem system (SIGIL); they cannot on their own establish encoded speech
verdict_per_comparator.reason: this is the DESIGN RATIONALE, not a competitor: it tells us the claim must be a genuinely predictive temporal property that beats a non-linguistic control. The structure claim is exactly that (a predictive held-out object-type property, dual-baseline, multi-site). It is the class SIGIL does NOT establish (SIGIL is the control's model, not a temporal object-type prediction).

summary: The structure claim (temporal M77->post-1977 object-type predictability, dual-baseline, multi-site, paired-bootstrap) is not equivalent to any P1-P9, Q1-Q14, R1-R13, Mahadevan 1977, Rao/Yadav 2009-10, or Kriger-Hunt 2026 property, and is the class the SIGIL paper (2608.02999) establishes as NOT covered by the standard statistics.
closest_comparator: Q13 (stability over time) — a time effect, but an in-sample rate-bound, not a predictive dual-baseline held-out accuracy; and P7/K-H edge-entropy (the non-specific positional class, which the claim deliberately avoids).
